parsed.notes:
The 'Minimum qualifications' items are required. Everything under the 'Preferred qualifications' heading is nice_to_have.
'ML or software engineering experience' could be read as an alternatives pair. Each skill is also asked for on its own ('building and evaluating ML systems'; 'reliable production software development'), so both leave any group.
'Transformers' is most likely the Hugging Face library. The taxonomy only has the architecture entry `transformers`, which matches the name literally, so I used it and flagged it.
PyTorch and Transformers are grouped because the bullet offers them as alternatives ('or comparable ML libraries'). 'or comparable' adds no skill.
In 'human evaluation, LLM-as-judge calibration, recommendation metrics or online experimentation', the evaluation items collapse into the required `evaluation` criterion, so evaluation leaves the group.
Within that same list, recommendation metrics maps to `recommender-systems` and online experimentation maps to `a-b-testing`. Both mappings are loose and flagged; I grouped the two because of the 'X, Y or Z' wording.
'language-model training or post-training' maps to `llms` plus `fine-tuning`, with post-training treated as fine-tuning; both are flagged. They are not grouped because the two are not clean alternatives of the same skill.
The tech in the responsibilities section (LLM-based graders, tool calls, dashboards, agents) and in the company description is not labeled.
